Rudloff.et: Derived from a variation of the given name Rudolf. The name consists of the stems "hruod" which means honour or renown and "wolf" which means wolf.

Rudolf.et: From Middle High German Rudolf, from Old High German Ruodolf, from Proto-West Germanic *Hrōþiwulf.

Rüde.et: From Middle High German rüde, rüd, from Old High German rudio, from Proto-Germanic *hruþjô (“male dog”), possibly from *hruttōn- (“to roar”), from a Proto-Indo-European root shared by Ancient Greek κόρυζα (kóruza), Old English hrot. Or, from Proto-Germanic *hr…

Rüdiger.et: From Middle High German Rüedeger, from Old High German Ruodigēr, from Proto-West Germanic *Hrōþigaiʀ, from Proto-Germanic *Hrōþigaizaz. Cognate with English Hrothgar and Roger.

s: a surname originating as a patronymic

s: to row (propel over water using oars)
rudern.et: From Middle High German ruodern, from Old High German ruoderōn, garuoderōn, ultimately related to Proto-Germanic *rōaną (“to row”). Also see Ruder.

rudimentär.et: Borrowed from French rudimentaire, from French rudiment, from Latin rudimentum.

s: a native or inhabitant of Rüdesheim

Ruderwettkämpfer.et: Ruderwettkampf (“rowng competition”) + -er; equivalent to rudern (“to row”) + Wettkämpfer (“competitor”)

From Rudel (“pack of animals, throng”) + Bildung (“formation”).
